QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_38

question.text: Investor-level risk called 'Risk of Adverse Selection' in AIFs refers to:

answer.text: Credit risk of a single investee
The risk that the investor may choose a sub-optimal fund manager based on forward-looking PPM claims that may not materialise
Market risk from the underlying portfolio

explanation.text: The Logic: Adverse selection risk = the difficulty of picking the right manager based on backward-looking track records and forward-looking PPM promises that don't guarantee future performance. It's an INVESTOR-level risk (not fund-level). The Trap: A/C/D are distinct risk types discussed separately in Chapter 7. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B Cat III Distributor frames adverse selection from advisor angle. XIX-E tests from manager's PPM-disclosure perspective. Manager's Pro-Tip: Include manager-background, team-biographies, and worst-case-scenario fund examples in the PPM. Transparent disclosure reduces adverse-selection complaints and future litigation risk.
